transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Lately I’ve been overwhelmed by guilt about letting everyone down at home and at work, even when people tell me it’s not that bad. I just feel like I'm constantly failing, and I can't seem to shake this heavy feeling that I'm disappointing everyone.
Have you been feeling this level of guilt almost every day for at least two weeks, and has it affected your ability to work or do daily activities?

Yes, I've been feeling this intense guilt almost every single day, and it has actually been dragging on for about five months now. It has severely impacted my life; I've been missing deadlines and forgetting meetings at work to the point where my team has to pick up my slack, and I keep backing out of plans with my family.
Before this current period of guilt and low mood, did you have any similar episodes in the past, or has this been the first time you've felt this way?

No, this isn't the first time. I've actually had these cycles of feeling highly energized for a few weeks and then sinking into these long, drained stretches happening on and off for at least a few years. They've just become much more noticeable recently with the extra stress at home and work.
During those times when you felt highly energized, did you also experience a decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, or impulsive behavior like excessive spending or risky decisions?

Yes, during those weeks I would sleep for only about four hours but wake up feeling completely wired, with my thoughts racing three steps ahead of what I was saying. I didn't have issues with reckless spending or risky decisions, but I did impulsively overcommit myself to a ton of new work projects and community events that I couldn't actually handle.
During those energized periods, did you feel your mood was unusually high, irritable, or expansive—different from your usual self, even if it felt good at the time?

Yes, I felt unusually upbeat and was constantly buzzing with ideas, but I was also really touchy. I'd find myself joking around one minute, and the next I'd snap at my daughter over something minor and wonder why I overreacted. It was definitely a big shift from how I normally am.
